fixes.explanation: Yes, friend! Jesus says, “…it is for the glory of God, so that the Son of God may be glorified through it.” He names God and the Son of God right there. It's the reason He gives, and I'll stick to what He actually said.

That's a fair guess, friend, but it isn't what Jesus says. He says the sickness is “…for the glory of God, so that the Son of God may be glorified through it.” The text doesn't call it a test of Mary and Martha. I'd have guessed a test too, and I'd have been just as wrong as you.

Good thinking, friend, but a village lesson isn't what Jesus says. He doesn't mention the village at all. What He says is that it's “…for the glory of God, so that the Son of God may be glorified through it.” Nobody in that sentence is getting a lesson, only God and His Son are named.

The text says the opposite, friend. When Jesus says to go back to Judea, the disciples answer, “Rabbi, the Jews just tried to stone You, and You are going back there?” So they do remind Him, and right away. I think that one question holds all their worry.

A kind idea, friend, but that isn't what Jesus says. He tells the disciples, “…I am going there to wake him up.” He's talking about traveling to Lazarus, not staying put. Praying from here never comes up in this passage.

Creative, friend, but no dream appears in this story. John says Jesus “…was speaking about the death of Lazarus.” The disciples took Him to mean actual sleep, and the real meaning was far heavier. I think this part of the story hurts.
